title: Longer noise blocks raise fixed-period null tail fractions for GJ 433 in 86 HARPS exposures
abstract: We test the known 36.059-day GJ 433 wave in 86 HARPS-RVBank version 02 exposures. Conditional residual sign tests give fixed-period tail fractions of 0.002, 0.090, and 0.200 for 1-, 30-, and 90-day groups. A main time validation fit favors the published period over two annual aliases, but recovery tests show low validation power. A descriptive scan peaks at 35.22 days in SERVAL and near 35.20 days in DRS. A scan after the known wave gives small conditional tail fractions, but shared spectra, simple baselines, and unknown activity noise prevent a new physical signal claim. No new planet or independent confirmation is established. The package contains code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure, and repeat steps. External source rows remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Left: descriptive full-fit period scan. Right: held-half error gains at three fixed periods. The scan maximum is selected on all data. Gains are conditional on nuisance refits. These statistics do not prove a planet.
